## Restored experiment and its relation to the mean-zero studies

This notebook restores a previously computed **nonzero-mean** zero-shift
experiment. It is separate from the corrected mean-zero `true_diff_*`
notebooks and from the single-sine zero-shift benchmark. It uses all nine
exponents $\alpha=0.9,\ldots,1.7$ and the same connected length-(1,2) tadpole.
The full archived numerical results are copied to a distinct filename;
restoring and knitting do not rerun the PDE computation.

Let $u_{\rm zero}$ denote the solution with the original smooth mean-zero data.
Here the initial condition and forcing are
$$
 u_0^{\rm added}=1+\frac{10}{\sqrt{16}}\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}e_j,
 \qquad f^{\rm added}(s,t)=1+10\sin(\pi t)e_7(s),
 \qquad \mathcal J=\{5,6,8,\ldots,21\}.
$$
At $\kappa=0$, the Kirchhoff fractional Laplacian annihilates constants, so
$$
 u_{\rm added}(s,t)=u_{\rm zero}(s,t)+1+t,
 \qquad \bar u(t)=1+t,\qquad M(t)=3(1+t).
$$
This identity holds for any of the reported alpha values and diffusion
coefficients. It describes the same centered diffusion with an additional
uniform component supplied by the forcing. The positive-mode initial norm
is 10; the full initial norm is $\sqrt{103}$. The total mass increases because
the forcing has mean 1.

At matching FEM and BE parameters, the numerical solutions satisfy
$$
 U_{\rm added}^k=U_{\rm zero}^k+(1+t_k)\mathbf1
$$
in exact arithmetic. The solver handles this constant component exactly
through the separate mean recurrence; it does not approximate it using BRASIL.

## Running and knitting

1. Run setup and parameters before making a new computation.
2. Run the computation chunk manually only when you want a new result.
3. Knit to load the restored or newly computed result and redraw plots.

The computation chunk has `eval=FALSE`. Missing results or incompatible
scientific settings stop knitting with a manual-run instruction. Internal
tests remain in `DOCS/NAP`; no test suite runs during knitting.

```{r nonzero-mean-conv-in-m-isolated-setup}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message=FALSE,warning=TRUE,error=FALSE,cache=FALSE,
                      dev="png",fig.width=8,fig.height=5)
if(!requireNamespace("ggplot2",quietly=TRUE)) stop("Install ggplot2 for the figures.")
```

## Explicit parameters of the restored full run

The defaults below match the archived numerical run. They are not silently
replaced with the current mean-zero study's defaults. `workers` affects
execution only. All outputs have a distinct `nonzero_mean_` prefix.

```{r nonzero-mean-conv-in-m-isolated-parameters}
T_final <- 1
kappa <- 0
gamma_star <- 1/3
alpha_vector <- seq(0.9,1.7,0.1)
diffusion <- 1
h <- 0.02
tau <- 0.005
m_vector <- 2:16
workers <- 1L
K <- 16L
initial_modes <- c(5L,6L,8:21)
initial_amplitude <- 10
forcing_amplitude <- 10
initial_mean <- 1
forcing_mean <- 1
AAA <- 1
OMEGA <- pi
stopifnot(length(initial_modes)==K,!(7L %in% initial_modes))
output_file <- "data_files/nonzero_mean_conv_in_m_isolated.rds"

# Bundle only the visible parameters above for the shared runner.
settings <- list(study="m",T_final=T_final,kappa=kappa,gamma_star=gamma_star,
    alpha=alpha_vector,diffusion=diffusion,workers=workers,initial_modes=initial_modes,
    initial_amplitude=initial_amplitude,forcing_amplitude=forcing_amplitude,
    initial_mean=initial_mean,forcing_mean=forcing_mean,A=AAA,omega=OMEGA,h=h,tau=tau,m=m_vector)
settings_table <- data.frame(parameter=names(settings),
    value=vapply(settings,function(x) paste(x,collapse=", "),character(1)))
knitr::kable(settings_table)
```

## Reference solution, mean splitting, and error interpretation

The smooth continuum solution contains the original 17 active positive eigenmodes and an
additional basis function one with coefficient 1+t. Analytical sine/cosine
hat integrals assemble the initial projection and spatial loads. The
sine forcing is averaged exactly over every BE interval, and the constant
forcing contributes the load C*one. The fixed gap scale is gamma*=1/3.
At each step the complete load is split as
$$
 v=CU^k+\tau(F_{\rm sine}\overline g_{k+1}+C\mathbf1),
 \quad q=\frac{\mathbf1^Tv}{3},\quad b=v-qC\mathbf1.
$$
The shifted sparse solves act on b; the returned vector is the centered
result plus $q\mathbf1$. Here $q=1+t_{k+1}$, up to roundoff. The algorithm and its
code mapping are documented in `kappa0func.Rmd`, Section 4.1.

This study compares sparse rational BE with exact-discrete BE on the
same FEM mesh, projection, load, and time grid. Both have the identical
constant component 1+t_k. Consequently the added component cancels from
$$
 E_m^2=\tau\sum_{k=1}^N
 (U_h^k-U_{h,m}^k)^TC(U_h^k-U_{h,m}^k).
$$
The isolated rational errors are therefore the same as in a mean-zero run
with matching parameters, in exact arithmetic. Small differences between
saved runs can arise from floating-point arithmetic. The complete discrete
eigensystem supplies the independent BE reference; constants have exactly
zero eigenvalue. The numerical-noise control and resolved-order indicator
have the same interpretation as in the mean-zero isolated-m notebook.
Fit ln(E_m) against sqrt(m); the root-exponential reference exponent is
-2*pi*sqrt(alpha/2), not an imposed observed slope.

## Choice of settings for reporting

The full order range m=2:16 is retained: every saved point was resolved
above the numerical-noise indicator and every curve decreased. The
integer-power control and FEM-eigenbasis comparison are reported below.
The constant cancels in this discrete-BE error, so adding the mean does
not create a temporal error floor here. No settings are changed merely
to make fitted slopes match the root-exponential reference guide.

## Computation

This is an optional explicit rerun, not part of knitting. The saved
restored result is already available. A rerun writes only this notebook's
own output path, leaving the mean-zero experiments and the archive intact.

```{r nonzero-mean-conv-in-m-isolated-recompute, eval=FALSE}
for(package in c("Matrix","rSPDE","Rcpp","RcppEigen"))
    if(!requireNamespace(package,quietly=TRUE)) stop("Missing package: ",package)
true_diff <- local({
    extracted <- tempfile("nonzero_mean_functions_",fileext=".R")
    on.exit(unlink(extracted),add=TRUE)
    knitr::purl("kappa0func.Rmd",output=extracted,quiet=TRUE,documentation=0L)
    functions <- new.env(parent=globalenv())
    sys.source(extracted,envir=functions)
    functions
})
result <- true_diff$kappa0_compute_study(settings,"nonzero_mean_conv_in_m_isolated.Rmd",output_file)
```

## Load saved results

```{r nonzero-mean-conv-in-m-isolated-load-results}
if(!file.exists(output_file)) stop("Saved nonzero-mean results are missing. Run setup, parameters, and recompute manually, then knit.")
result <- readRDS(output_file)
scientific_parameters <- setdiff(names(settings),"workers")
mismatch <- scientific_parameters[!vapply(scientific_parameters,function(name)
    isTRUE(all.equal(result$parameters[[name]],settings[[name]],tolerance=1e-12)),logical(1))]
if(length(mismatch)) stop("Saved settings differ for: ",paste(mismatch,collapse=", "),
    ". Run the computation chunk manually for these settings, then knit.")
restored_archive <- !("nonzero_mean_conv_in_m_isolated.Rmd" %in% names(result$source_hashes))
cat(if(restored_archive) "Restored archived computation; original generation time:" else "Computation generated:",
    result$generated_at,"\nSaved worker count:",result$parameters$workers,"\n")
```

## Results and fitted rates

The benchmark slopes describe the theoretical rate scale. The observed
fits use the computed data below; they are not replaced by the benchmark.
For smooth data, `max_mass_error` is the maximum absolute discrepancy from
the discrete mass recurrence over the entire trajectory. Here the expected mass grows as 3(1+t); the diagnostic checks its balance, not conservation.

```{r nonzero-mean-conv-in-m-isolated-rates}
knitr::kable(result$rates,digits=6)
```

```{r nonzero-mean-conv-in-m-isolated-plot-results}
d <- result$results
d$alpha_label <- factor(d$alpha,levels=settings$alpha)
if (settings$study=="m") {
    p <- ggplot2::ggplot(d,ggplot2::aes(sqrt(m),error,colour=alpha_label,group=alpha_label))+
        ggplot2::geom_line()+ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(shape=resolved))+
        ggplot2::scale_y_log10()+ggplot2::labs(x="sqrt(m)",y="Isolated space-time L2 error",
            colour="alpha",shape="Resolved",title="Zero-shift rational convergence: nonzero mean")
} else {
    p <- ggplot2::ggplot(d,ggplot2::aes(axis,error,colour=alpha_label,group=alpha_label))+
        ggplot2::geom_line()+ggplot2::geom_point()+ggplot2::scale_x_log10()+
        ggplot2::scale_y_log10()+ggplot2::labs(x=if(settings$study=="tau") "tau" else "h",
            y="Sampled space-time L2 error",colour="alpha",title="Zero-shift convergence: nonzero mean")
}
# Reference curves retain their prescribed slope and are geometrically
# anchored to the data. They are guides, not additional computed errors.
guides <- do.call(rbind,lapply(settings$alpha,function(a) {
    x <- d[d$alpha==a,]
    power <- if(settings$study=="m") -2*pi*sqrt(a/2) else if(settings$study=="tau") 1 else 2
    xx <- if(settings$study=="m") sqrt(x$m) else log(x$axis)
    if(settings$study=="rough_h") power <- a
    x$guide <- exp(mean(log(x$error)-power*xx)+power*xx)
    x
}))
guides$alpha_label <- factor(guides$alpha,levels=settings$alpha)
p <- p+ggplot2::geom_line(data=guides,ggplot2::aes(y=guide),linetype="dashed",alpha=0.6)+
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size=12)+ggplot2::labs(subtitle=sprintf("kappa=0; gamma*=%g",settings$gamma_star))
print(p)
figure_dir <- "data_files/nonzero_mean_conv_in_m_isolated"
dir.create(figure_dir,recursive=TRUE,showWarnings=FALSE)
ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(figure_dir,"convergence.pdf"),p,width=8,height=5)
```

### Source approximation and numerical-noise diagnostics

```{r nonzero-mean-conv-in-m-isolated-direct-power-figure}
u <- result$unit_errors
u$alpha_label <- factor(u$alpha,levels=settings$alpha)
power_plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(u,ggplot2::aes(sqrt(m),error,colour=alpha_label))+
    ggplot2::geom_line()+ggplot2::geom_point()+ggplot2::scale_y_log10()+
    ggplot2::labs(x="sqrt(m)",y="Sampled direct-power error",colour="alpha")+
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size=12)
print(power_plot)
ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(figure_dir,"direct_power.pdf"),power_plot,width=8,height=5)
knitr::kable(result$control,digits=12,caption="Integer-power control: no rational approximation")
knitr::kable(result$spectrum,digits=12,caption="Discrete spectrum diagnostics")
```

The restored RDS is a byte-for-byte copy of the archived full result,
including its original computation timestamp, source hashes, and package
versions. The original source hashes refer to the earlier notebook names;
they are retained as historical provenance and are not relabeled as a new
computation. The restoration manifest is in
`DOCS/NAP/true_diff_internal/restored_nonzero_mean_checks`.

If you edit parameters, run the manual computation chunk to generate a new
result at this notebook's own output path, then knit again. A new run will
record the current helper and this notebook as its sources. The archive is
retained, so the original computation remains recoverable. No profile or
recompute option causes simulations to run while knitting.
